current_profile.mode: native Windows editor --debug --profiling with candidate release EXE as --main-pack

normalization.method: For each sampled combat frame, divide self/inclusive milliseconds and call counts by Movement._physics_process calls / 200. This tick estimate equals ProjectileSystem._physics_process and FogOfWar._physics_process call counts in every current and prior sampled combat frame. Report the arithmetic mean of these per-frame ratios, with absent functions contributing zero.
normalization.timing_units: Profiler seconds converted to milliseconds; self_us_per_call uses total self / total calls.

findings: Spatial queries and movement remain the dominant recurring script work: nearby_units and Battlefield._refresh lead self cost; _on_velocity_computed leads inclusive cost.
Service reuse is visible in calls: power_totals falls from 7.7167 to 1.05 calls/tick. RepairService inclusive time falls from 1.5062 to 0.3839 ms/tick in these samples.

Unit._get_movement_speed calls fall from 333.1333 to 68.3/tick; Movement.speed from 969.75 to 721.35/tick. Movement._physics_process self time falls from 0.5352 to 0.3312 ms/tick, while its callback is still about 0.927 self / 5.885 inclusive ms/tick.
Battlefield._refresh self per call is 3.8418 us prior versus 2.6701 current; nearby_units remains around 1.261 self ms/tick, so query enumeration is still a concrete investigation target.

BastionVisuals._advance_pose runs 280 times per sampled rendered frame in both profiles, with 0.9685 versus 0.9629 self ms/frame. Its larger current per-tick figure is a cadence artifact, not evidence of an animation regression.
CombatRobot._update_badge and DiagnosticHud._physics_process are absent from current sampled combat rows, consistent with normal-play diagnostic gating.
AuthoredSceneMap.overview appears in the top self list from only five calls across ten snapshots; treat it as periodic map/UI work, not a per-tick cost.
caveats: All seven native focus samples show Battle.net, not the game. No native foreground frame budget or p95 acceptance conclusion is supported.
This is an editor --debug --profiling run using the candidate EXE as --main-pack; profiler overhead changes cadence.
Inclusive costs overlap through call trees and must not be summed. Ten sampled frames are not every simulation tick.
Per-render-frame functions must also be compared per frame/call: the prior samples contain more physics ticks per rendered frame.
Different sampled battle states and focus conditions prevent causal speedup claims; call-count shifts provide stronger attribution evidence than timing ratios.
